labels.label: ex:following_situations_semi_locally_simply

hypotheses.paper: §3 standing: Y Hausdorff, connected, LPC, first countable

hypotheses.note: E any nontrivial real normed space (n >= 1)
local models in any finite-dimensional E of dimension >= 2
locally polygonal up to local homeomorphism (GX.IsLocallyPolygonal); unruled

hypotheses.paper: item 3: Y a simplicial complex of dimension n
hypotheses.note: every face in a face with >= n vertices (GX.HasFacesOfCardGe); false as written (connected counterexample GX.following_situations_simplicial_false); locally finite geometric complex with the subspace topology
DEC-55 literal compact-open reading: GX.following_situations_finite_cc, _tame_cc, _tame_knot_cc, _simplicial_cc (a fortiori from the homotopy form)

findings: l.1564 (item 3) is false as written: a connected complex of dimension n can have a maximal face of dimension <= n-2, then Y minus the (n-2)-skeleton is not dense (GX.following_situations_simplicial_false). True when every face lies in a face with >= n vertices (pure complexes in particular).
l.1562 (item 1): n >= 2 is not needed; n >= 1 suffices.
l.1563 (item 2): neither dimension 3 nor being a knot is used: any locally polygonal closed set in a manifold of dimension >= 2 works.
questions: Reading of 'tame knot' (l.1563) as locally polygonal up to local homeomorphism (GX.IsLocallyPolygonal) — accept? (unchanged from WP-26h; no ruling yet)
Accept the correction of item 3 (every face in a face with >= n vertices) and the restriction to locally finite complexes (as DEC-57 did for rem:simple_cases)?

labels.label: ex:consider_denote_absolute_galois

hypotheses.note: DEC-58: the normal closure GX.gamma2 (the printed one is all of Gamma, GX.printedGamma2_eq_top)

hypotheses.paper: 'the fibre above (0,0) in Y_2 is a Cantor set'
hypotheses.note: FALSE (not compact); strongest true form proved (DEC-27): the fibre is infinite (pairwise distinct ends GX.absGalEnd_injective), totally disconnected (cor:totdiscont through the spread Γ₂\\Ũ → ℂ, GX.isSpread_homeoQuotient_lift, for any Γ₂) and not compact: GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_corrected_simple (general form GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_corrected). Perfectness (no isolated point) not formalized

unconditional refutation for the explicit loops GX.absGalSimpleLoop n at y0 = -i/4 (segment, circle of radius 1/(2(n+1)(n+2)) around 1/(n+1), segment back; windings GX.absGal_windAt_simpleLoop); these lollipops are homotopic to based simple closed curves around 1/(n+1) (Schoenflies), not formalized. General theorem GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_not_compact: any gamma_0, gamma_1 with odd winding around {1, 1/2}, any gamma_n (n >= 2) inside GX.absGalR (which contains Re z < 1/2)
DEC-55 literal reading: GX.absGal_not_isSLSCInCC (via GX.isSLSCInCC_iff, C minus S open and semilocally simply connected)

findings: l.1571, first claim, proved in the literal reading (DEC-55): C minus S is not semi-locally simply connected in C (GX.absGal_not_isSLSCInCC).
l.1572: the printed Gamma_2 = <Gamma [gamma_n]^2 Gamma> is all of Gamma (GX.printedGamma2_eq_top); DEC-58 reads the normal closure.

l.1573 is FALSE (DEC-27), now PROVED, unconditionally: with Gamma_2 the normal closure of the squares of the simple loops, the fibre above (0,0) of Y_2 is NOT compact, hence not a Cantor set (GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_not_cantor_simple; sorry-free, axioms propext/choice/Quot.sound). Proof: a dihedral invariant of the universal cover of C minus S — continuous logarithms l of F = (z-1)/(z-1/2) and Lambda of G(exp(l/2)), G(s) = (s-1)/(s+1); deck transformations act by (sq, Lambda) -> (±sq, ±Lambda + c); the squares of the loops around 1 and 1/2 and the loops in absGalR act trivially, so Gamma_2 does; a loop around {1, 1/2} translates Lambda by ±2πi; the integer Theta = (Lambda - (sq/sqrt F) log G(sqrt F))/(2πi) is locally constant over the disc D_5 (radius 2/11) and separates infinitely many components of its preimage in Gamma_2 \ universal cover, each reached by an end over 0, which gives an open cover of the fibre with no finite subcover. (The WP-26h sketch used a different quotient; this one needs only the two points 1, 1/2.)

l.1573, corrected (DEC-27): what survives of 'Cantor set' is proved — the fibre above 0 of Y_2 is infinite and totally disconnected, but not compact (GX.absGal_Y₂_fiber_corrected_simple, sorry-free). Whether it is perfect is not formalized.
l.1573: a Cantor fibre would be obtained with Gamma_2' = kernel of the mod-2 winding numbers around the 1/n (an abelian quotient); not formalized.

l.1573: 'answers positively Problem 10.7 of MR2198590' is bibliographic and not formalized; since the fibre is not a Cantor set, the claimed answer to Montesinos's problem does not follow from this example as written.
questions: The paper's gamma_n are formalized as the lollipop loops GX.absGalSimpleLoop (homotopic to based simple loops); accept, or should a homotopy with an embedded simple loop be formalized?
Is a corrected example intended (e.g. Gamma_2' = kernel of the mod-2 windings, giving a Cantor fibre), or should the example be withdrawn? The current statement is refuted.

labels.label: ex:wild_cantor_general_antoine

hypotheses.paper: S a wild Cantor set [general_antoine] in S^3
hypotheses.note: DEC-58: Antoine's necklace, BUILT explicitly: GX.antoineNecklace (inverse stereographic image GX.antoineStereo of GX.antoineNecklaceR3 = ⋂ₙ GX.antoineStage n, chains of 64 interlocking square solid rings GX.antoineLink placed by the similarities GX.antoineMap of ratio 7/80), proved a Cantor set (GX.antoineNecklace_isCantorSubset, sorry-free). The claim is stated FOR THIS NECKLACE (GX.antoineNecklace_wild_not_isSLSCInCC), not merely for some wild Cantor set (the existential forms GX.exists_wild_cantor_not_isSLSCIn(CC) are corollaries), and not for every Antoine necklace (a general predicate would need a formal notion of linked solid tori; not defined)

hypotheses.paper: (cited, general_antoine) Antoine's theorem: the necklace is wild, its complement not simply connected
hypotheses.note: GX.antoineNecklace_antoine (wildness + essential meridian loops at every point), the only sorry of the file; the Cantor property is NOT cited but proved
DEC-55: the literal and homotopy forms agree for closed C in S^3 (GX.sphere3_isSLSCInCC_compl_iff), so the statement is in the literal form

sorries.obstruction: Antoine's theorem for the explicit necklace (whose Cantor property, nesting and the pairwise disjointness of the 64 links of each generation are PROVED). Missing: (1) the essential loop — a meridian of a link L of generation n is not null-homotopic in S^3 minus (C ∩ L). No abelian invariant can detect it (H^1 of the complement of a closed subset of a Cantor set vanishes by Alexander duality, so winding/linking numbers, maps to S^1 and abelian covers all give 0); by compactness of a null-homotopy it suffices to detect it in the complement of each finite stage C_m ∩ L (64^(m-n) solid tori), which needs for every m a non-abelian covering/representation of π₁ of that complement (an iterated lift, the depth-2 instance of which is the dihedral invariant of ex:consider_denote_absolute_galois, or Antoine's van Kampen computation); mathlib has neither van Kampen nor π₁ of a solid-torus complement. (2) Accessibility: a path from each x ∈ C to the meridian meeting C only at x. (3) Wildness: a Cantor set carried into a great circle has a semi-locally simply connected complement, which needs the simple connectivity of S^3 minus a compact subset of a circle (again van Kampen-type).

findings: Under DEC-58 the example is about Antoine's necklace, now constructed (GX.antoineNecklace) and the statement made about it; the general wild-Cantor reading (refuted in WP-26h modulo Kirkor's existence) is only a side remark (GX.wild_cantor_claim_false_of_exists, proved).

The geometry of the construction is checked mechanically: all 64×64 pairs of first-generation links are box-separated except the 64 cyclically consecutive pairs (GX.antoine_sep_or_adj, GX.antoine_adj_succ, by decide), and consecutive ones are disjoint (GX.antoine_link_aux); that consecutive links are genuinely LINKED is read off the coordinates and is used only inside the citation.
questions: The claim is stated for one explicit Antoine necklace (square rings, 64 links per chain, ratio 7/80). Antoine necklaces are not all ambient-equivalent (Sher 1968), though Antoine's theorem holds for each; is the explicit necklace an acceptable reading of DEC-58, or is a statement over every Antoine necklace (a predicate on nested chains of linked tame solid tori) wanted?

kb_proposals: Non-abelian invariants of a planar complement without van Kampen: on the universal cover (GX.UniversalCover, simply connected and LPC for an open subset of C) take a continuous log l of F∘p through mathlib's exp covering (IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts with Complex.isCoveringMap_exp), then a log Lambda of G(exp(l/2)); deck transformations act on (exp(l/2), Lambda) through (±1, affine), which gives an infinite-dihedral representation of pi_1 (GX.absGal_deck_action). Compute the action of a loop class through UniversalCover.liftFrom and explicit lifts (GX.absGal_deckHom_base, GX.absGal_expLift_eq).

Components of a preimage in a quotient H\X̃: a function on X̃ that is H-invariant and locally constant over an open set descends through Quotient.lift and is constant on connected components (GX.IsPreconnected.subset_of_pairwise_disjoint on its level sets; openness via isQuotientMap_quotient_mk'.isOpen_preimage).

Ends over a point: build a FiberThread on the basis range fibD from lifted vertical segments (GX.absGalThread) and use FiberThread.toEnd; non-compactness of a fibre follows from an infinite family of ends with pairwise distinct components over one connected neighbourhood (cover by SpreadEnd.basicSet).
Winding numbers: cWinding of s ⬝ c ⬝ s⁻¹ equals cWinding c (GX.absGal_cWinding_conj); winding of a pointwise quotient is the difference (proof of GX.absGal_cWinding_F).

S^3 = sphere in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) is LocPathConnected via `import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Sphere`, a local Fact (finrank = 3 + 1) and ChartedSpace.locPathConnectedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) _.
Under `open unitInterval`, σ is notation: never use σ as a bound variable name (identifiers like absGalσ are fine).

A quotient of a spread by a group of homeomorphisms over the base is a spread (GX.isSpread_homeoQuotient_lift): components of preimages in H\\X are images of components in X, since H permutes the latter; with GX.isTotallyDisconnected_fiber this gives total disconnectedness of fibres of Fox completions of H\\Ũ → Y.

Finite geometric case checks over a fixed configuration (64×64 pairs of boxes) go through kernel `decide` on integer data (coordinates scaled to ℤ) in seconds; cast to ℝ with exact_mod_cast. No native_decide needed.

An IFS attractor ⋂ₙ ⋃_w (g_{w₀}∘⋯∘g_{w_{n-1}})(L) with contracting injective maps and disjoint first-stage pieces is ≃ₜ (ℕ → ι) by the coding map (limUnder of the orbit of a base point; continuity via cylinders Set.pi (range n) {w k}); (ℕ → Fin 64) ≃ₜ (ℕ → Bool) via Fintype.equivOfCardEq, Equiv.curry and Nat.divModEquiv (GX.antoineFin64Homeomorph).
